headline: Oil Prices Rebound Amid Renewed Middle East Supply Concerns
summary: Crude oil prices rebounded from four-week lows as traders shifted focus back to the Middle East conflict, with Brent crude trading at $103.60 per barrel.
why: Crude oil is a vital global commodity and energy input, with its price directly influencing inflation, transportation costs, and the margins of energy-intensive industries worldwide.

impacts.name: Brent crude
impacts.why: The input explicitly states that Brent crude was trading higher at $103.60 per barrel following the rebound.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Oil prices rebounded as traders shifted attention from U.S. midterms to Middle East supply fears, driving benchmarks up from four-week lows.
